original_question: Let M be a closed manifold not covered by a sphere.
target_in_paper: Section 8.9, Question 8.9.1, "Metrics such that all geodesics are closed."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the opening topological hypothesis of the paper’s target question: M is a closed manifold, and the sphere-covered cases are excluded.
missing_details: The paper’s question is in the Riemannian setting, so one must introduce a Riemannian metric g on M.
The key hypothesis is missing: all geodesics of g are closed.
Using the paper’s standing notation, geodesics are the arclength-parametrized curves γ_v determined by v in SM unless otherwise specified.
The actual yes/no rigidity question is missing: whether (M, g) must be a CROSS.
CROSS must be expanded as "compact rank one symmetric" manifold, exactly as the paper does.
Section 1 supplies hidden standing assumptions that M is connected and C^∞.
The conclusion "with the standard metric" is part of the paper’s official formulation and should be retained.
As written, the draft is only a hypothesis fragment, not yet a stand-alone research question.
refined_question: Let M be a connected closed (compact without boundary) C^∞ manifold that is not covered by a sphere, and let g be a Riemannian metric on M such that every arclength-parametrized g-geodesic is closed. Must (M, g) be a compact rank one symmetric manifold equipped with its standard metric?
justification: The draft is aiming at the exact rigidity problem stated in Section 8.9 as Question 8.9.1. The nearby context shows that this is the Riemannian version; Finsler and Lorentzian analogues are mentioned only as separate variants, so they should not replace the target question. Section 1 supplies the paper’s standing conventions needed to make the question fully stand-alone: M is connected and smooth, and γ_v denotes the arclength-parametrized geodesic determined by v in SM.
